newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hitachi group aims at 1 trln yen DVD sales.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi group aims at 1 trln yen DVD sales.

text.p: Hitachi Ltd said on Wednesday that the Hitachi group aims to achieve annual digital video disk (DVD) related sales of one trillion yen in five years, or about 2002.
Hitachi and its unit Hitachi Maxell Ltd started sample shipments of DVD-RAM drives and disks on Wednesday.
Hitachi Maxell aims at a market price of about 5,000 yen per unit for its DVD-RAM disks when they start volume production, expected around the end of this year.

Hitachi said the one-trillion yen sales target will include home-use DVD players and recorders, electronic goods such as televisions and personal computers that include DVD devices, parts, drives, disks and recording and publishing services related to the production of digital video disks.

DVD-RAMs allow users to enter and rewrite a large volume of data and images, including motion pictures. The disks offer more flexibility than non-rewritable DVD-ROMs, in which the stored data is fixed and cannot be replaced.
Electronics manufacturers like Hitachi expect that DVD-RAMs will replace CD-ROMs, which are currently a major memory device in personal computers.
